method: the same OMR, extraction, traversal, compilation and render, run on a public-domain score by a different composer with a different structure. The traversal became a parameter; nothing else changed.
question: does the A1-02 score pipeline work on a score it was not built for?

scores.name: Children (A1-02)
scores.role: the score the pipeline was built for
scores.structure: repeats, alternate endings, Segno, To Coda, D.S. al Coda
scores.traversal_source: A1-02's own module, derived from the printed markers

scores.name: J.S. Bach, WTK I Prelude No. 1, BWV 846
scores.role: a score the pipeline had never seen
scores.structure: no repeats, no endings, no Segno, no Coda; ratio 1.0
scores.traversal_source: read from its own notation by traversal.from_score

the_one_change_required: compile_performed imported A1-02's traversal. A traversal belongs to the piece, not to the compiler, so it became a parameter defaulting to A1-02's. The tempo rule that keeps a commercial recording's pulse out of score extraction is also A1-02's, and a score with no such control has nothing to be protected from.
what_did_not_generalize: OMR glyph recognition missed the Segno, the Coda and one forward repeat on the A1-02 score, so its traversal still comes from an independent reading of the page rather than from the transcription
the engineering piano is one caricature voice for any score
